line: A: Is it affecting every device in the house, or only one of them?
C: It's not just one device, put it that way.
A: Can you tell me what lights are showing on the front of the equipment right now?
C: There's a power light, and then one that keeps blinking. I couldn't tell you what it means.
A: Has anything changed at home recently? New equipment, building work, anything like that?
C: No, nothing. It's all exactly as it was last week.
A: Are you connected by Wi-Fi or with a cable when you see the problem?
C: Wi-Fi mostly. I haven't got a cable anywhere handy.
A: Did it stop all at once, or has it been getting gradually worse?
C: All at once, I think. One minute it was fine and then it wasn't.
A: Do you have a landline with us too, and is that working?
C: We don't use the landline, so I honestly couldn't say.
A: Roughly where in the property is the equipment kept?
C: In the hall, on a shelf by the front door. It's always been there.
mobile: A: Is this happening wherever you go, or only in one place?
C: Everywhere I've been today. Home, work, the shops.
A: What kind of phone are you using, and is it the one you bought from us?
C: It's a couple of years old. I got it from you with the contract.
A: Is anyone else in your household on our network, and do they have the same trouble?
C: My partner is, and hers is doing exactly the same thing.
A: Have you changed handsets recently, or is it the same phone as last month?
C: Same phone. I haven't changed anything on it.
A: Are you calling me from the affected phone at the moment?
C: No, I've borrowed a different phone to ring you.
A: Does the phone show the Meridian network name at the top of the screen?
C: It does, yes. It looks perfectly normal, which is the strange part.
A: Have you travelled abroad with the phone in the last few days?
C: No, I've not been anywhere.
tv: A: Is it the same on every channel and every programme, or only some?
C: Most of them, as far as I can tell. I've tried quite a few.
A: Which room is this in, and do you have more than one screen with us?
C: It's the living room one. We've only got the one.
A: Is the television itself working normally with other things, like a games console?
C: Yes, everything else plugged into the telly is fine.
A: Do you see any message or code on the screen when it goes wrong?
C: Something flashes up, but it's gone before I can read it.
A: Was it working properly earlier in the week?
C: Yes, perfectly. We watched a film on it at the weekend.
A: Is your home internet working normally for everything else?
C: It seems to be. My phone's fine on the Wi-Fi.
A: Has anybody changed any settings recently, or moved any cables?
C: Not that I know of. The grandchildren might have, but I doubt it.
online: A: Are you using a computer, a tablet or a phone when this happens?
C: My phone mostly, but I tried another device too and it was the same.
A: Do you get an error message, and can you read me what it says?
C: Nothing that tells me what's actually wrong, put it that way.
A: When did you last manage to use it without a problem?
C: A few days ago, I think. It was fine then.
A: Are you on your home connection or a different one, like at work?
C: At home, on my own Wi-Fi.
A: Have you changed your password or any security details lately?
C: No, I've left all that alone.
A: Is anyone else you know having the same trouble?
C: My sister is with you as well, and she said hers was playing up.
A: Is it every time you try, or does it sometimes work?
C: Most times, yes. I must have tried ten times before ringing.

line: A: Let's try a full restart first. Could you switch the equipment off at the wall, leave it for thirty seconds, and switch it back on?
C: OK, doing that now. Right, it's off.
A: Lovely. Give it the full thirty seconds, because it needs to clear its memory.
C: Back on. The lights are coming up one by one.
A: It can take a couple of minutes to settle. Tell me when they stop flashing.
C: They've stopped. It's exactly the same as before, though.
A: Can you check the cable that goes from the equipment to the wall socket? Make sure it's pushed in firmly at both ends.
C: Hang on, I'll have to move the bookcase. Yes, it's in tight at both ends.
A: Thank you. And is there any damage along the cable, any kinks or chew marks?
C: No, it looks fine to me.
A: OK. That rules out the simplest explanation.
C: I didn't think it would be that, to be honest.
A: I'm going to run a line test from here. It takes about a minute, and your connection may flicker while it runs.
C: It can't flicker much more than it already is.
A: Fair enough. The test is running now.
C: OK.
A: Right, the test has finished. It hasn't found a fault on the line into your property, which tells me the problem is further back.
C: So it's not my house, then.
A: Do you have a computer you could plug straight into the equipment with a cable? It would tell us whether the Wi-Fi is the weak point.
C: I've got an old laptop and a cable somewhere. Give me a second.
A: Take your time.
C: Right, it's plugged in. There's no difference at all. Still the same.
A: Thank you, that's useful. So it isn't a wireless problem.
A: Could you look at the label on the equipment and read me the serial number? I want to check it's registered correctly.
C: It's tiny writing. It starts with a nine and ends in four four two, if that helps.
A: That matches our records, thank you. The equipment is registered and showing as the right model.
C: So that's not it, then.
A: No. Everything on the account side looks correct.
A: I'd like to send a refresh signal to your equipment. It only takes a moment, and you don't need to touch anything.
C: Go on, then.
A: That's been sent. Could you try again now, and tell me what you see?
C: One second. No, no change. It's doing the same thing.
A: OK. Thank you for trying.
mobile: A: Could you turn flight mode on, wait ten seconds, and turn it off again? It makes the phone register with the network afresh.
C: OK. It's on. And off again.
A: Thank you. Give it a moment to find the network.
C: The bars have come back, but it's still not working properly.
A: Understood. That tells me the phone can see the mast.
A: When did you last restart the phone completely? Not just locking the screen, but powering it right off.
C: I couldn't tell you. Weeks ago, probably.
A: Let's do that now, if you don't mind. Hold the power button and choose restart.
C: It's restarting. OK, it's back on now.
A: And how is it?
C: The same, I'm afraid. No better.
A: I'd like you to take the SIM card out, give it a gentle wipe, and put it back in. Do you have the little pin for the tray?
C: I've got a paper clip. Will that do?
A: That works just as well.
C: Right, the SIM is out. It looks clean. It's going back in now.
A: Let the phone settle for a minute, and then try again.
C: No change. It's still doing the same thing.
A: In the settings, under mobile network, is the network selection set to automatic?
C: Let me look. Yes, it says automatic.
A: Good. And is the option for 4G or 5G switched on?
C: Yes, that's on as well.
A: Then your settings are as they should be. It's not a configuration problem on the handset.
A: I'm going to send your phone a fresh set of network settings. You'll get a message asking you to install them.
C: OK. Something's just come through.
A: Tap install or accept on that message.
C: Done. It says the settings were installed.
A: Could you try again now?
C: Still the same. Nothing's changed.
A: Do you have another phone you could put your SIM into, just as a test?
C: There's my old one in a drawer. Hold on.
A: Thank you. I know it's a nuisance.
C: Right, the SIM is in the old phone, and it's exactly the same on this one.
A: That's very helpful. It means the handset isn't the problem.
tv: A: Let's restart the device first. Could you hold the power button until it switches off completely, and then turn it back on?
C: It's going off. And it's back on now.
A: Give it a minute to load fully.
C: OK, it's loaded. It's no different, though.
A: Thank you for trying. That's the first thing ticked off.
A: Could you check the cable between the device and the television? Unplug it at both ends and push it back in firmly.
C: Right. I've done both ends.
A: And is the television on the right input for it?
C: Yes, it's on the same input it's always on.
A: OK. So the connection to the screen is fine.
A: I'd like you to sign out of your TV account on the device and sign back in. Do you know your details?
C: I think so. Let me try. OK, I'm signed out.
A: Now sign in again with the same email and password.
C: I'm back in. It's still doing the same thing.
A: All right. At least we know your sign-in is working.
A: Can you go into settings, then system, and tell me the software version that's shown?
C: It's a long number. It ends in point seven.
A: That's the current version, so you're up to date.
C: So it's not that I've missed an update.
A: No, nothing is outstanding on your device.
A: I'm sending a refresh signal to your equipment now. The screen may go blank for a few seconds.
C: Yes, it's gone black. Now it's back.
A: Good. Could you try what you were doing before?
C: Same again. No improvement.
A: Thank you. I've noted that the refresh didn't help.
A: Does the same thing happen if you use our app on a phone or a tablet, instead of on the television?
C: I've not tried. Give me a second to open it on my phone.
A: Of course.
C: It's the same on my phone, actually.
A: That's useful to know. It suggests the fault isn't with the equipment in your living room.
online: A: Could you close the browser completely and open it again? Then go straight to our site, rather than using a bookmark.
C: OK. Closed. Opening it again now.
A: Thank you. Try signing in when the page comes up.
C: Same result as before.
A: All right. So it isn't a stuck page.
A: Let's try clearing the saved data for our site. In your browser settings there's an option for cookies and site data.
C: I think I've found it. Clear data for this site?
A: That's the one. Go ahead and confirm.
C: Done. I'm trying again now. No, it's exactly the same.
A: OK. That rules out old data on your computer.
A: Do you have a different browser or another device that you could try?
C: I've got a tablet here. Hold on a moment.
A: Thank you.
C: It's doing the same on the tablet.
A: Right. Then it's not specific to one device, which is helpful to know.
A: Could you check that the date and time on your device are correct? It sounds odd, but it can cause this.
C: They look right to me. It's set to automatic.
A: Good. That's another possibility ruled out.
C: I'd never have thought of that one.
A: It catches a lot of people out, but it isn't the answer today.
A: I'm going to reset your session from my side. You'll be signed out everywhere, and then I'd like you to sign in again.
C: OK, I've been thrown out to the sign-in page.
A: That's expected. Sign in as normal for me.
C: Right. No, it's still not working.
A: Thank you. I've recorded that the session reset made no difference.
A: Could you remove the app and install it again from the store? You won't lose anything, because it's all held on your account.
C: Deleting it. Installing. It takes a minute.
A: No problem at all.
C: It's back, and I'm signed in. Same as before, I'm afraid.
A: OK. So it isn't a damaged copy of the app.
